rounds.summary: Seven acceptance criteria verified, no failure, one ledger finding: two go-test lines the implementer quoted for AC1 and AC3 were from the pre-simplify head's run rather than from the job they cited.

The reviewer's six minor findings were folded into this round rather than deferred. I re-verified every criterion at this head and drove the three things this round actually changes in behaviour a consumer meets: the `--check` guard's new GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT redirect, that running the gen-go tests no longer mutates the shared workspace's tracked generated files, and the controller skill's new report budget. No failure; one note about that budget's wording against its live proof.

implementerProof.how: Round 2. Every quoted observation in the new handoff was checked against the job it cites, because round 1's one finding was exactly this: `gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 119503157551 --log` (envoy-go, run 39680934534) prints `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/api 510.192s` and `ok .../outbox 42.371s`; job 119503157645 (dispatch) prints the three body-cap rows, `cli-body-cap.e2e.ts:91:1 ... (761ms)`, `composer-body-cap.e2e.ts:25:1 ... (2.3s)` and `:54:1 ... (1.2s)`, with `1442 passed (42.4m)`; job 119503538565 (test, run 39680934528) prints `ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/daemon 325.401s` and `ok .../internal/workflow 160.837s`. Every one matches the handoff's quote exactly, at head e6b6f23c — round 1's stale-quote defect did not recur. The surfaces this pod can run I drove again at this head rather than carrying round 1's observations forward: both generated-file guards with hand-edited tracked copies, the new GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT paths (missing root, faithful copies, stale copy), the gen-go test suite with the tracked files hashed before and after, `bun run check-dist`, the compiled daemon constants, the reader-tab guard, and the real `dispatch` command against the live INFRA Dispatch. Round 1's verdict and its correction stand in the `rounds` entry above and in the pull request body.

proof.command: gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 119503157551 --log (run 39680934534), plus a read of the new packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/body_cap_margin_test.go at this head.
proof.observed: `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/api 510.192s` at e6b6f23c, with both TestBodiesAreCappedOnEveryWriteRoute and the new TestAnchoredCommentAtTheBodyCapReachesTheMarginWhole compiled into it. The margin test asserts equality of the margin record's text against the whole body sent, not a length or a prefix, so a projection that summarised or truncated would fail it; its 256 KiB and 1 MiB byte budgets are unchanged by this diff and match growth.go:149,155. In CI: gh run view --repo sjawhar/legion --job 119503157645 --log.

proof.criterion: The review round's workspace-safety fix - running the generated-file checks must not mutate the tracked files every role of this issue shares, and the new GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT redirect must not weaken the guard.
proof.surface: The real scripts in this pod: `packages/contracts/scripts/gen-go.ts --check` and `bun test scripts/gen-go.test.ts`, against the shared issue workspace itself.
proof.command: `sha256sum` of both generated files before and after `bun test scripts/gen-go.test.ts`; `GEN_GO_CHECK_ROOT=/tmp/emptyroot bun run scripts/gen-go.ts --check`; the same with a faithful copy tree; the same with one copy made stale; and `bun run check:go` with the variable unset.
proof.observed: `3 pass, 0 fail` in 719 ms, and both tracked generated files byte-identical before and after (`jj status`: no change) - the hazard the reviewer named, a killed run leaving a tracked Go file hand-edited in a workspace six roles share, is gone. The redirect behaves: a faithful copy tree exits 0, a copy made stale exits 1 naming the copy's path under the temporary root, and the variable unset still compares the committed files and still fails on a hand-edit of either. It does not fail open: pointed at an empty root the check exits 1 with `ENOENT ... /tmp/emptyroot/packages/envoy/internal/contracts/generated.go`, rather than passing because it found nothing to compare.
proof.negativeControl: The empty-root run above is the fail-open control (exit 1, not 0), and the stale-copy run is the positive one (exit 1 naming the stale file). The guard's real mode was controlled the same way: a hand-edit of each committed file with the variable unset, each refused by name.

notes: One note, not a failure, for the architect rather than the implementer. The controller skill now reads `under about 2,000 characters` for the daily report, while the two artefacts that prove it assert a hard bound: stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:5461 requires `(.payload.body | length) <= 2000` and scripts/e2e/README.md:1452 says `within 2,000 characters`. A controller obeying `about 2,000` with a 2,050-character report would fail that live proof after its 300 s wait. Before this round the skill said `at most 32,000` and the proof asserted `<= 32000`, so the soft/hard mismatch is new. It bites only the devbox Stage 4b run, nothing in CI, and the budget itself is the right change; the cheap fix is one word in the skill (`at most 2,000`) or a margin in the proof.

Round 1's finding is closed: this round's eight quoted observations each appear verbatim in the job cited, at the head cited. The round-1 correction (the implementer's AC1/AC3 lines quoting run 39655628814 job 119415067575 at head 76c1eb9c) stands in the record above; the lines themselves were corrected in the pull request body as the architect directed.

The deploy skew is still measurable rather than theoretical: at this head the real `dispatch message` sent a 32,000-unit body and the live INFRA Dispatch refused it `body is 30000 characters over the 2000-character limit (32000/2000)`, so production carries the old cap and the production check after the merge will meet that (dispatch://INFRA-64 is the deploy gap).

The margin consequence this round documents is bounded as written: the anchored comment reaches the margin whole (new Go test), the byte budgets are untouched, and the refusal past them is a clean 413 with the transaction rolled back. No test pins the 256 KiB record bound itself; the architect ruled that out of scope for this change, since pinning it honestly needs three full-cap replies and the bound is pre-existing.
